Ph.D. Programs
The three graduate fields - Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, and Theoretical and Applied Mechanics - cross traditional college and department boundaries and afford a graduate student maximum flexibility in designing a program represented by faculty from virtually any discipline on campus. We also offer a doctoral degree program in Robotics in both Mechanical Engineering and Mechanical Engineering.

Why the Sibley School of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering?
Flexibility
The four graduate fields cross traditional college and department boundaries and afford a graduate student maximum flexibility in designing a program represented by faculty from virtually any discipline on campus.
Collaboration
Cornell Engineering is known for its radical collaboration across departments, colleges and campuses. Collaboration allows our students and faculty to accelerate discovery – leading to impactful and lasting change.
Exceptional Faculty
Faculty in the Sibley School conduct cutting-edge research in a wide array of areas including robotics, space science, and health care to name a few.
The Sibley School Ph.D. Program Difference
First Semester Fellowship
Most students do not choose a Ph.D. advisor before applying. Matriculated students on first semester fellowships are afforded the opportunity to interact with a number of faculty in seeking a good student-advisor match within the first semester.
Grad Student Community
Prospective graduate students are drawn to the Sibley School by the close community of multi-cultural and diverse graduate students. Students feel as though they are part of an inclusive community that supports one another throughout the Ph.D. process.
Five Years of Funding
We offer five years of funding to all admitted Ph.D. students (contingent upon maintaining good academic standing).
Student-Led Graduate Research Symposium Exposes Possibilities and Strengthens Skills
Each year, the student-led organization SiGMA (Sibley Graduates in Mechanical and Aerospace) holds an annual research symposium, funded by industry and academic sponsors.
An important component is networking with a panel of career professionals in academia, industry, startups, and national labs to represent the wide variety of careers students in mechanical and aerospace engineering end up in.
This year, in addition to prizes for the most clearly communicated research presentations, students were invited to compete for the best artistic rendition of their research.
The day’s activities included a career panel, a skills workshop, graduate research talks, and a reception that gave students the opportunity to connect with peers, faculty, and professionals in a more informal setting.
The Cornell Career Network published a story about the 2026 SiGMA Symposium.
